answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can join the marketplace, and to tie that bond to a verifiable reputation thread linking its past trades, endorsements, and disputes. Newcomers are not banned, but they start with limited harbor capacity: they can only hold a few open deals until peers attest to reliable behavior. Creating fake identities is then expensive, because each sock puppet needs its own bond and must slowly wander through real, checkable transactions to earn trust, while misbehavior forfeits the bond and stains the whole thread.
